result.title: Correlational Training of Morphological Neural Networks
result.summary: Neural networks are typically trained using first-order methods and back-propagation. It is unclear whether this approach is optimal for morphological layers whose weight Jacobians are sparse and whose resulting parameter gradients can be poor. In this work, we propose a novel weight update method for morphological neural networks inspired from the Multiplicative Weights Update (MWU) scheme. We view each morphological perceptron as an instance of the learning from experts' advice problem in logarithmic space, and use a correlation-based reward that favors inputs aligned with the desired output change, regardless of whether a strong gradient signal has reached their weight. We empirically evaluate our approach by training fully connected layers both as stand-alone models and as parts of larger transformer networks. Across nine benchmarks, correlational training yields improvements on eight, by up to 32.84 percentage points, while substantially reducing run-to-run variability.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文针对形态学（morphological）层权重雅可比稀疏、梯度质量差的问题，提出一种受乘性权重更新（MWU）启发的相关性权重更新方法，并在九个基准（含 transformer 内部层）上验证其效果与稳定性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「以输入与期望输出变化的相关性作为奖励、不依赖强梯度是否到达权重」的信用分配思路，可能为 latent 推理轨迹训练中梯度稀疏或信号弱的监督与贡献分配问题提供借鉴线索，可供核查。
